title: Per-tenant burst bucket reset semantics and post-billing reconciliation
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Goal: define and implement deterministic reset semantics for per-tenant burst buckets (short-term burst credits) while preserving correct monthly/daily quota accounting for reserved capacity customers, and provide a reconciliation path that ensures invoices match observed usage. Background: we currently support rolling-window quotas and anchored daily/monthly quotas in different subsystems which leads to edge cases around bursts that cross window boundaries, clock skew between region controllers, and reserved-capacity onboarding where committed units must not be double-billed. This ticket covers design, implementation, and validation of a hybrid approach: - Use a leaky-bucket style burst bucket with a configurable accrual rate (credits/sec) per tenant. - Keep the burst bucket as a rolling window (sliding decay) to allow transient bursts without abrupt resets. - Anchor accounting for billable quotas (monthly/daily) to UTC-aligned boundaries for invoicing clarity. - On reserved capacity, maintain a separate committed pool counter and an overage counter; overages are recorded against burst usage but reconciled at billing. - Implement event-sourced usage ledger entries for every token-use that can be replayed to reconcile between runtime counters and billing aggregates. Rationale: rolling burst buckets preserve UX for latency-sensitive features, while anchored billable quotas provide straightforward invoicing and reporting. Event-sourcing avoids race conditions when aggregating distributed counters and is the core of the reconciliation story.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by billing + infra + PM
Implementation emits event-sourced usage records for all token billing-relevant operations
Burst bucket behavior passes synthetic burst tests across region-controller clock skews up to 5s
Monthly invoices match aggregated ledger within 0.1% for a 72-hour reconciliation window
Reserved-capacity customers show zero double-billing in end-to-end test scenarios
comments: 2025-02-12: Spike complete. Two approaches tested: anchored credits reset at UTC midnight vs rolling decay. Rolling decay wins for UX but needs ledger reconciliation for billing.
2025-02-18: PM (Jordan Marks) requested explicit overage visibility on Console cost breakdown for reserved capacity. Added UI task to follow-up.
2025-02-25: Engineering review: distributed counter drift observed during chaos tests (leader failover). Decided to introduce per-region checkpoints to bound divergence.
2025-03-01: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3124 implementing event-emitter and ledger writes. Needs load-test validation before merge.
2025-03-04: Design feedback from Finance: require replay window of at least 30 days for auditability. Added retention + compaction note to design doc.
steps_taken: Completed spike (2025-02-12) comparing decay vs anchored reset semantics under synthetic traffic patterns
Built simulation harness that replays 30 days of tenant traffic and compares invoice deltas between designs
Implemented prototype event-sourced ledger in a feature branch and ran local integration with billing-aggregator
Ran chaos tests for leader failover and region clock skew using ci-load-2 synthetic cluster
decision_log: Decision 2025-02-18: Use rolling decay for burst buckets (leaky-bucket) to avoid hard rate-limiting cliffs for latency-sensitive tenants.
Decision 2025-02-25: Anchor billable quotas (daily/monthly) to UTC midnight for downstream invoicing and customer clarity.
Decision 2025-03-03: Persist every billable token usage as an append-only ledger event to enable deterministic reconciliation and auditability.
Trade-off: increased storage and write amplification vs. stronger correctness guarantees and auditable invoices. Acceptable for initial rollout under billing-2025.03.
